title: Ephemeral Inference Sandbox — Legal Guardrails Template
content:
Purpose:
This template creates a short-form legal and operational annex for customers and vendors who require a time-limited, isolated inference sandbox ("Ephemeral Inference Sandbox") for integration testing, model validation, or third-party eval. The goal is to enable realistic testing while limiting data residency, retention, and access surface, and to provide a clear audit trail for compliance teams.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to ephemeral sandbox environments provisioned either by Redwood or by an approved vendor when processing any customer-provided or customer-simulated queries.
- Intended for non-production usage: development, integration, benchmarking, and third-party model evaluation. Not for production inference or handling of live personal data unless explicitly agreed and annotated in Appendix A.

Key definitions (examples to adapt):
- "Sandbox Instance": a short-lived environment provisioned for a customer or partner for the purpose of testing.
- "Ephemeral Data": any input, intermediate artifacts (KV caches, attention context), and outputs generated within a Sandbox Instance.
- "Sanitized Test Data": test inputs that have been reviewed and pseudonymized to remove direct identifiers.
- "Retention Window": the maximum time Ephemeral Data may persist in any system or backup before automated deletion.

Control objectives (high level):
1) Data minimization: limit the set of customer-supplied inputs used in the sandbox; prefer sanitized test data.
2) Temporal isolation: Sandbox Instances must self-destruct or be destroyed by operator action at the end of the agreed window.
3) Access limitation: restrict human and service access to the minimal set of named personnel and processes.
4) Forensic transparency: capture an audit trail sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the agreed controls, with short retention where possible.

Contract clauses (boilerplate items; edit to fit negotiation):
1. Provisioning and Term:
  a) Redwood (or Provider) will provision Sandbox Instances on request for internal testing or third-party evaluation as described in the Order Form. The Parties will agree on the start timestamp and the Duration (not to exceed [insert maximum days]).
  b) Sandbox Instances are expressly limited to the stated purpose. Use outside that purpose requires prior written approval. Unauthorized promotion of instances to production is prohibited.

2. Data handling and retention:
  a) Customer may supply Production-Like data only if expressly authorized in Appendix A and must mark such data as "PRODUCTION-LIKE". In the absence of explicit authorization, Customer will supply only Sanitized Test Data.
  b) Ephemeral Data will be automatically deleted from the primary environment and any attached caches within the agreed Retention Window (default: 24 hours after sandbox termination) and purged from backups within 30 days unless otherwise negotiated.
  c) The Provider will not use Customer Ephemeral Data to train or improve models except with explicit, opt-in written consent. Any use for model improvement must be documented and auditable.

3. Access, personnel, and secrets:
  a) Provider will implement least-privilege access for humans and services interacting with Sandbox Instances. Personnel access must be pre-approved by Customer for third-party vendors and logged.
  b) Where keys or secrets are required, the Parties will prefer customer-owned KMS or short-lived credentials provisioned via an agreed mechanism. Long-lived credentials are prohibited in sandbox contexts.

4. Logging, telemetry, and telemetry minimization:
  a) Provider will capture only minimal telemetry necessary for provisioning, billing (if any), and security. Telemetry fields are listed in Appendix B.
  b) Where logs may contain customer query payloads or outputs, those logs will be masked at capture time or truncated and will be subject to the Retention Window.

5. Audit and evidence:
  a) Provider will maintain an auditable record of Sandbox Instance lifecycle events (create, start, stop, destroy), personnel access events, and retention/deletion events for at least 90 days, unless a shorter period is specified in Appendix C.
  b) Provider will deliver a sandbox evidence package on request within [30] business days containing: provisioning metadata, deletion certificates, and a redacted activity log.

6. Security controls and baseline requirements:
  a) Network isolation: Sandboxes must be deployed in logically isolated VPCs or equivalent segmentation with restricted egress rules.
  b) Host and runtime hardening: Instances shall run with limited privileges; container images or host images must be scanned for critical vulnerabilities prior to provisioning.
  c) Patch cadence: Critical security fixes applied within [X] days; other security patches per Provider policy.

7. Incident response and breach notification:
  a) If a security incident affects Ephemeral Data, Provider will notify Customer within the incident notification timeline in the Master Agreement (e.g., 72 hours) and provide remediation steps and evidence of containment.

8. Subprocessors and third-party vendors:
  a) Provider will not engage subprocessors to access Ephemeral Data without Customer pre-approval for the specific vendor and purpose. Subprocessor approvals may be handled via a pre-approved vendor list appended to Appendix D.

9. Liability and risk allocation:
  a) Provider liability for Ephemeral Data exposure is subject to the general limits of liability in the Master Agreement. Parties may negotiate narrower caps for test environments; if Customer requires higher limits this must be explicitly added to the Order Form.

10. Certification and attestation:
  a) Provider will provide a periodic (quarterly/annual) attestation that sandbox controls were applied for the term requested. Attestations include deletion certificate templates and sample audit logs with redaction.

Operational playbook (recommended provisions to include as an attachment):
- Pre-provisioning checklist: data classification, approved personnel list, required scan reports, test data sanitization proof.
- Provisioning runbook: template commands or API calls, required environment variables, KMS integration steps, expected resource quotas.
- Termination runbook: explicit commands to purge KV caches, clear accelerator-local ephemeral storage, revoke credentials, call deletion API and capture deletion certificate.
- Evidence bundle template: JSON with instance_id, start_time, stop_time, deletion_time, deletion_token, list_of_access_events (redacted).

Negotiation tips for legal/Sales/CS teams (practical):
- Customers often ask to keep logs longer for debugging. Offer a compromise: longer evidence retention in a separate attestation repository that is access-controlled and does not include raw payloads.
- If Customer insists on using production data, require a one-off dataclass and approval process (appendix A), and a higher-liability or insurance layer.
- Insist on test data sanitization controls as a precondition to any longer retention.

Appendices (suggested):
- Appendix A: Authorized Production-Like Data Exception Form (fields: justification, responsible engineer, retention exception duration, required safeguards).
- Appendix B: Telemetry schema for sandboxes (list of allowed fields, hashed vs plaintext, mask rules).
- Appendix C: Evidence and retention schedule (derived from the Master Agreement).
- Appendix D: Pre-approved sandbox subprocessors and approval workflow.

Sign-off block (placeholder):
For Customer:  ______________________  Name: [Customer signatory]
For Provider (Redwood Inference):  ______________________  Name: Ava Martinez, Head of Security & Compliance

Notes to drafter:
- Keep this annex short and checklist-like; most customers want a simple yes/no on key points (duration, production-data allowance, liability uplift).
- Cross-reference Master Agreement sections on confidentiality, security obligations, and incident reporting rather than duplicating generic language.
- Coordinate with SRE/Platform to confirm the practical deletion guarantees for accelerators (GPUs) and local NVMe devices to ensure the deletion certificate is meaningful.

Change history:

- 2024-12-02: added telemetry minimization section (Noah Patel)
